The Nagoya Protocol (NP) is an international agreement that aims to share the benefits resulting from the utilization of genetic resources fairly and equitably. To learn more about it and if it is related to your research, you can check the German Nagoya Protocol Hub here: https://www.nagoyaprotocol-hub.de/

The MIxS standard (Minimum Information about any (x) Sequence) is an overarching framework providing a single entry point to all minimum information checklists from the Genomic Standards Consortium (GSC) and to the environmental packages. MIxS includes the technology-specific checklists from the previous MIGS (Minimum Information about a Genome Sequence) and MIMS (Minimum Information about a Metagenome Sequence) standards. It provides a way to introduce additional checklists, such as MIMARKS (Minimum Information about a Marker Gene Sequence), and allows annotation of sample data using environmental packages. MIxS was published in Nature Biotechnology in 2011.
More about the MIxS standard here: https://genomicsstandardsconsortium.github.io/mixs/

The ISO 19115-1:2014 Geographic information (Metadata) is a standard of the ISO (the International Organization for Standardization) and defines the schema required for describing geographic information and services by means of metadata. It provides information about the identification, the extent, the quality, the spatial and temporal aspects, the content, the spatial reference, the portrayal, distribution, and other properties of digital geographic data and services.
More about the ISO 19115-1:2014 Geographic information (Metadata) here: https://www.iso.org/standard/53798.html

The INSPIRE Directive aims to create a European Union spatial data infrastructure that will help to make spatial or geographical information more accessible and interoperable for a wide range of purposes of EU environmental policies and policies or activities which may have an impact on the environment. On 15 May 2007, the INPIRE Directive came into force and will be implemented in various stages, with full implementation required by 2021.
More about INSPIRE here: http://inspire.ec.europa.eu/about-inspire/563

The Europeana Semantic Elements (ESE) is a format that provides a basic set of elements for describing objects in the cultural heritage domain in a way that is usable for Europeana.
More about the Europeana Semantic Elements  here: https://pro.europeana.eu/page/ese-documentation

The Ecological Metadata Language (EML) is a set of XML Schema documents that allow for the structural expression of metadata necessary to document a typical data set in ecological sciences.
More about the Ecological Metadata Language here: https://eml.ecoinformatics.org/

The Europeana Data Model (EDM) aims to be an integration medium for collecting, connecting, and enriching the descriptions provided by Europeana content providers.
More about the Europeana Data model here: https://pro.europeana.eu/page/edm-documentation

The Darwin Core (DwC) is body of standards. It includes a glossary of terms intended to facilitate the sharing of information about biological diversity by providing reference definitions, examples, and commentaries. The Darwin Core is primarily based on taxa, their occurrence in nature as documented by observations, specimens, and samples, and related information. DwC is an accepted standard of Biodiversity Information Standards (also known as Taxonomic Databases Working Group).
More about Darwin Core here: https://dwc.tdwg.org/

Dublin Core (DC) is a metadata standard that was originally developed for libraries but its elements have been reused in many other formats as well, e.g. DWC. Dublin Core Metadata Element Set contains 15 elements and is an accepted ISO standard (ISO 15836:2009).
More about Dublin Core here: https://www.dublincore.org/resources/metadata-basics/

The Access to Biological Collections Data (ABCD) schema is the core standard for any BioCASe-related network. Its primary use case is the publication of rich natural history collections' specimen data, but it can also be used for general species occurrence datasets. It is XML-based (eXtensible Markup Language), meaning it stores the information in a structure that can be easily processed by software. The current major version, 2.06, has been widely adopted by networks and is an accepted standard of the Biodiversity Information Standards (also known as the Taxonomic Databases Working Group).
More about ABCD here: https://abcd.tdwg.org/

fields.help_lang1: The overall goal of GFBio is to provide a sustainable, service-oriented, national data infrastructure facilitating data sharing. Thus, we support the idea of open access to data. Attaching a corresponding license to your data is an important part of data management. Open access does not mean everyone can use your data at their leisure. Data can be cited, as well as publications can be. Licenses define citation demands as well as further terms of use, e.g., if data may be remixed or transformed. You can check all the Creative Commons Licenses options here: https://creativecommons.org/share-your-work/cclicenses/
fields.help_lang2: Das übergeordnete Ziel von GFBio ist die Bereitstellung einer nachhaltigen, serviceorientierten, nationalen Dateninfrastruktur, die den Datenaustausch erleichtert. Wir unterstützen daher die Idee des offenen Zugangs zu Daten. Eine entsprechende Lizenzierung Ihrer Daten ist ein wichtiger Teil des Datenmanagements. Open Access bedeutet nicht, dass jeder Ihre Daten nach Belieben nutzen kann. Daten können ebenso zitiert werden wie Publikationen. Lizenzen definieren Zitationsforderungen sowie weitere Nutzungsbedingungen, z.B. wenn Daten transformiert werden können.

fields.help_lang1: Will your data meet any ethical issues or legal requirements such as personally identifiable information? Data dealing with abundance of Red List Species needs to be handled according to the legal requirements and may not be easily published. In terms of handling genetic resources, the Nagoya Protocol has to be considered. If you feel uncertain about legal requirements, choose 'uncertain' and we support you in identifying your legal requirements.
fields.help_lang2: Erfüllen Ihre Daten alle ethischen und rechtlichen Anforderungen, wie z.B. persönlich identifizierbare Informationen? Daten, die sich mit der Fülle der Arten der Roten Liste befassen, müssen entsprechend den gesetzlichen Bestimmungen behandelt werden und dürfen möglicherweise nicht ohne Weiteres veröffentlicht werden. Hinsichtlich des Umgangs mit genetischen Ressourcen ist das Nagoya-Protokoll zu beachten. Wenn Sie sich bezüglich der rechtlichen Anforderungen unsicher fühlen, wählen Sie "unsicher" und wir unterstützen Sie bei der Ermittlung Ihrer rechtlichen Anforderungen.

fields.text_lang1: Are you a member of a research unit (Forschungsgruppe)?

fields.help_lang1: Please describe the data management coordination of your programme. Who takes care of it? Is there a data management plan, guideline or policy on which all project members agree? If there are any documents available, please refer to them (by upload, link DOI or full citation).
fields.help_lang2: Bitte beschreiben Sie die Koordinierung der Datenverwaltung Ihres Programms. Wer kümmert sich darum? Gibt es einen Datenmanagementplan, eine Richtlinie oder eine Politik, auf die sich alle Projektmitglieder einigen? Falls Dokumente vorhanden sind, verweisen Sie bitte auf diese (durch Hochladen, Link DOI oder vollständige Zitierung).
fields.text_lang1: If you are part of a coordinated programme (Koordinierte Programme, Verbundprojekte), is there any specific coordination, guideline or policy for data management?
fields.text_lang2: Falls Sie Teil eines koordinierten Programms (Koordinierte Programme, Verbundprojekte) sind: Gibt es eine spezifische Koordination, Richtlinien oder Bestimmungen für das Datenmanagement?

fields.help_lang1: Funding agencies or even funding programmes demand certain data management standards. We support you in meeting their requirements.
fields.help_lang2: Finanzierungsagenturen oder sogar Finanzierungsprogramme verlangen bestimmte Datenverwaltungsstandards. Wir unterstützen Sie dabei, deren Anforderungen zu erfüllen.
fields.text_lang1: For which funding are you applying?
fields.text_lang2: Für welche Finanzierung bewerben Sie sich?

fields.help_lang1: You can combine several types.
fields.help_lang2: Sie können mehrere Arten kombinieren.
fields.text_lang2: Bitte spezifizieren Sie die Art Ihres Projekts

fields.text_lang1: Add additional information (e.g. data reproduction might cause high costs or a lot of effort)
fields.text_lang2: Zusätzliche Informationen hinzufügen (z.B., dass die Datenreproduktion hohe Kosten oder einen großen Aufwand bedeuten könnte)
